name: District of Columbia
$methodComment: Genuinely the SIMPLEST bracket shape in this project structurally, despite DC's real-world reputation for a steep top rate (10.75%): ONE bracket table for every filing status (like Rhode Island), and the ONLY reduction is a flat per-ALLOWANCE dollar amount subtracted BEFORE the bracket lookup -- no separate standard deduction line at all in the withholding formula (unlike the RETURN-level DC-1040, which does have a large standard deduction; several secondary sources conflated the two, the same withholding-formula-vs-return-level distinction already caught for California/Utah/Colorado in this project). D-4's own allowance count folds self/HOH/age/blind/spouse/dependents into ONE number, all valued identically at the same per-allowance dollar figure -- unlike DC's own field name ('Dependent Allowance = $X x Number of Dependents' in NFC's formula), the count is NOT literally dependents-only; it's the FULL D-4 Line total.

sources.title: USDA National Finance Center -- District of Columbia Income Tax Withholding (NFC-22-1668460546, still NFC's current DC formula in 2026)
DC Department of Employment Services, Office of Paid Family Leave -- Employer Information
sources.quote: On July 1, 2024, the Paid Family Leave (PFL) tax rate increased from 0.26% (0.0026) to 0.75% (0.0075) of the wage paid to each covered employee

sources.title: U.S. Department of Labor, ETA -- Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective January 2025

bracketAnnualAllowanceDeduction.bracketsComment: Verbatim from the NFC formula, and internally chain-verified before trusting it: 400 + (40000-10000)x0.06=400+1800=2200 (matches); 2200+(60000-40000)x0.065=2200+1300=3500 (matches); 3500+(250000-60000)x0.085=3500+16150=19650 (matches); 19650+(500000-250000)x0.0925=19650+23125=42775 (matches); 42775+(1000000-500000)x0.0975=42775+48750=91525 (matches) -- every published base independently reproduced from the one before it, zero discrepancies. ONE table for all filing statuses.
bracketAnnualAllowanceDeduction.allowanceAmountComment: STALENESS DISCLOSED, not hidden: this figure is from the 2022 NFC bulletin ('the annual deduction amount has changed from $4,150 to $4,300') -- no 2026-dated confirmation of this SPECIFIC dollar figure was found this session, unlike the bracket thresholds (which WERE cross-checked against fresh 2026 sources and held up). DC's allowance amount plausibly adjusts periodically the way many states' does; this could be understating a 2026 figure that has since increased. Flagged explicitly as the single least-confident number in this file, rather than presented with the same confidence as the brackets.
bracketAnnualAllowanceDeduction.noCertificateDefault: Not explicitly stated in the sources found this session -- modelled as single/zero-allowances per this project's standing convention for a missing certificate (the least-generous outcome), NOT independently confirmed as DC's own stated rule the way Delaware's or Missouri's no-form defaults were.

exemptComment: DC's withholding formula itself is built on federal AGI-adjacent wages (subtract TSP/401k-style deferrals and pretax health benefits BEFORE annualizing, per the NFC formula's own Steps 1-3) -- the clearest, most directly-sourced exemptPretax basis of any state in this project except Arizona's A-4/Michigan's RAB-1988-27, since the WITHHOLDING FORMULA ITSELF spells out the subtraction steps rather than requiring an inference from a general AGI-conformity statute.

reciprocity.rule: STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from reciprocity everywhere else in this project: DC does not tax NONRESIDENT wages AT ALL, for residents of any of the 50 states, under a blanket federal prohibition (the 1973 Home Rule Act), not a bilateral agreement with specific named states. certificate.nonresident (a boolean, not a reciprocalStates list lookup) should zero DC withholding entirely for any employee who does not reside in DC, regardless of which state they DO reside in.
reciprocity.notModelledAsReciprocalStatesList: Deliberately NOT using this project's generic reciprocityExemptionReason()/reciprocalStates mechanism, because that mechanism checks residenceState.code against a closed LIST of specific states -- DC's actual rule is unconditional across all 50 states, which a finite list would have to (redundantly, and riskily forgettably) enumerate one by one. A dedicated nonresident check is the correct, not just convenient, way to model this specific fact.

localIncomeTax.rule: N/A -- DC has no sub-jurisdictions (no counties, no cities within DC) to levy a SEPARATE local tax; the DC income tax modelled above already IS the whole story, the same way NH/WA/etc.'s 'no income tax' entries are complete in themselves.

universalPaidLeave.$comment: DC Universal Paid Leave — 100% employer-funded, genuinely the only paid-leave program in this project with ZERO employee contribution. Computed as DC_PFML_ER via the statePaidLeaveEmployer block below — employerSizeGated:false, since DC's programme has no headcount threshold and every covered employer owes it.

verification: PROVEN via calculatePaycheck(): the bracket table's own internal base-chain was independently verified (see bracketsComment) before being used to hand-derive test fixtures, since no full worked example with a stated final dollar answer was found in the NFC bulletin the way California/Rhode Island's own sources provided. See tests/engine.test.ts, describe('District of Columbia').
knownGaps: Descriptive notes carried from the 2026 file (reciprocity, local-tax rules, method comments) were checked against the 2025 source for the fields this engine computes from; narrative text that only describes 2026 history should be read as background.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
suiEmployer.wageBaseSource: DOL Significant Provisions, January 2025 (Wages Subject to Tax)
suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: DOL Significant Provisions, January 2025 (New Employer Rate, base rate)

statePaidLeaveEmployer.$comment: DC Universal Paid Leave, wired from this file's own universalPaidLeave block: 0.75% of covered wages, funded 100% by the employer — the only paid-leave programme in this project with ZERO employee contribution. employerSizeGated is false because DC's programme has no headcount threshold at all: every covered employer owes it, so requiring a caller to assert liability first would just suppress a tax that is always due. No wage cap.

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset: the District's withholding formula (4% to 10.75% brackets, allowance deduction) is statutory and unchanged since NFC's October 2022 bulletin, which is still NFC's current DC formula. Universal Paid Leave has been 0.75% employer-only since 2024-07-01, so it applies to all of 2025.
